about: TE3 of docs/tasks/task-test-efficiency-2026-09.md. Read noise-registry.md beside this file first. sd and floor are in natural-log units of the ratio (0.01 ~ 1%) for every instrument except logits, whose entries carry a floor on their own metric (floor_value) and no sd. scripts/power.py reads this file; `power.py verify` recomputes every sd that has recorded values.

machines.mac: MacBook Pro M1 Pro, 16 GB, darwin/arm64 (Metal; CPU = arm64 NEON)
machines.nobara: nobara-pc: Ryzen 7 3700X (amd64, AVX2, no AVX-512) + RTX 2070 SUPER

served-decode.description: goinfer new / goinfer old decode tok/s through the server (scripts/bench_peer.py, and scripts/bench_splitkv.py / bench_spec_lane.py, which share its cell shape): a block is one cell per arm (a fresh server, one discarded warm-up, runs x 8 completions x 64 tokens)

served-decode-peer.description: goinfer / a peer (Ollama or llama-server) decode tok/s, same harness and block

served-decode-peer-arm.description: a peer engine against itself (the same Ollama / llama-server build in two cells): the peer's own A/A, an input to served-decode-peer

served-decode-xsession.description: the same build in two sessions (what a cross-session ratio silently carries; CLAUDE.md forbids such ratios for claims)

served-w7.description: scripts/bench_w7_plain.py aggregate tok/s (6 turns x 128 greedy tokens per client, a fresh server per cell), new / old, one pair per block

served-ttft.description: served prompt latency (time to first token), new / old: scripts/bench_peer_prefill.py or scripts/bench_prefill_stall.py

inproc-kernel.description: an in-process kernel or category A/B (a kernel bench, an ncu timing, a decomposition category), both arms in one process or alternating processes

inproc-token.description: an in-process whole-token decode A/B (BenchmarkDecode / BenchmarkResidentDecode / ABBA test hooks over production forward)

inproc-prefill.description: an in-process whole-prefill A/B (BenchmarkPrefillLong and the like)

logits.description: fidelity metrics (cosine, argmax agreement, KL, p10 cosine): entries carry a floor on the metric (floor_value), not an sd; use `power.py binomial` for agreement-rate sample sizes
